lesson.text: Quick memory: last unit, heat and temperature. Which way does heat always flow? From hotter things to colder things.

Kinetic energy is the energy of movement. The faster something moves, and the more mass it has, the more it has. A pendulum moves fastest at the bottom of its swing: its energy is kinetic there, and stored (potential) at the top.
When objects collide or push each other, energy is transferred: a moving ball hits a still one, slows down, and the still one starts to move.
Energy is never lost; it changes form or moves. When a skateboard slows down, some of its kinetic energy becomes heat and sound.
Stored energy can become kinetic energy: a stretched catapult, a ball held high, or a wound-up spring.
Try it in the world: ride down a hill in your world, or roll a boat down a slope into water. Where does the moving energy come from, and where does it go at the bottom? Next: energy changes.

exercises.prompt: What is kinetic energy?
exercises.hint: kinetic means moving.
exercises.explain: Kinetic energy is the energy of movement.

exercises.prompt: Which has more kinetic energy?
exercises.hint: Which one is moving faster?
exercises.explain: The faster it moves, the more kinetic energy.

exercises.prompt: A rolling ball has kinetic energy.
exercises.hint: It is moving.
exercises.explain: Yes: anything moving has kinetic energy.

exercises.prompt: A moving marble hits a still one. What happens?
exercises.hint: The still one starts to move.
choices: Energy passes to the still marble.
exercises.explain: Energy is transferred to the still marble.

exercises.prompt: Energy can be destroyed.
exercises.hint: Where does it go?
exercises.explain: No: energy changes form or moves, but is never destroyed.

exercises.prompt: Which has more kinetic energy at the same speed?
exercises.hint: They go at the same speed. Which one has more mass?
exercises.explain: The lorry has more mass.

exercises.prompt: A skateboard slows down on a flat path. Where does its energy go?
exercises.hint: Energy is never lost.
exercises.explain: Rubbing turns kinetic energy into heat and sound.

exercises.prompt: What kind of energy does a stretched catapult have?
exercises.hint: It isn't moving yet.
exercises.explain: It stores energy, ready to become movement.

exercises.prompt: When you rub your hands together, kinetic energy becomes heat.
exercises.hint: Your hands get warm.
exercises.explain: Yes: movement turns into heat.

exercises.prompt: A bowling ball hits the pins. What does the ball lose?
exercises.hint: The pins start to move.
exercises.explain: It gives some of its kinetic energy to the pins.

exercises.prompt: Why does a car need more braking to stop when it goes faster?
exercises.hint: Faster means more energy.
exercises.explain: More kinetic energy must be changed into heat to stop.

exercises.prompt: Order the energy changes when you drop a ball.
exercises.hint: Start before you let go.
items: sound and heat, hitting the ground
exercises.explain: Stored, then kinetic, then sound and heat.

exercises.prompt: In marbles, the shooter stops dead and the target shoots off. What happened?
exercises.hint: Energy moves from one to the other.
choices: The shooter gave its energy to the target.
exercises.explain: The shooter's kinetic energy was transferred to the target.

exercises.prompt: A heavier ball rolling at the same speed as a lighter one has more kinetic energy.
exercises.hint: Same speed, but which ball is heavier?
exercises.explain: Yes: more mass at the same speed means more kinetic energy.

exercises.prompt: Which design would make a toy car roll farthest after a push?
exercises.hint: Less rubbing wastes less energy.
exercises.explain: Less rubbing means less energy turned into heat.

exercises.prompt: Sort each one: moving energy (kinetic) or stored energy?
exercises.hint: Is it moving now, or ready to move?
exercises.explain: The rolling ball, running dog and flying bird are moving: kinetic. The catapult, the ball held high and the spring store energy, ready to move.

exercises.prompt: Match each event to its energy change.
exercises.hint: Start with the energy it has before, then what it becomes.
exercises.explain: Rubbing hands: kinetic to heat. A dropped ball: stored to kinetic, then sound as it lands. A catapult: stored to kinetic. A skateboard slowing: kinetic to heat and sound.

exercises.prompt: Watch the pendulum and its energy bars. Where does it have the most kinetic energy?
choices: at the bottom of its swing
at the top of its swing
exercises.hint: Kinetic energy is movement energy. Where is the pendulum moving fastest?
exercises.explain: At the bottom it moves fastest, so its kinetic energy is biggest. At the top it stops for a moment, and its energy is all stored.

exercises.prompt: Sort each energy change: stored to kinetic, or kinetic to heat or sound?
items: a ball rolls off a shelf
exercises.hint: Is something starting to move, or is something that moves slowing down?
exercises.explain: Starting to move uses stored energy: the catapult, the ball falling off the shelf, the wound-up toy. Slowing down turns kinetic energy into heat and sound: the skateboard, the brakes, rubbing hands.

exercises.prompt: Order them from the least kinetic energy to the most.
exercises.hint: More mass and more speed both mean more kinetic energy. Compare the bikes, then the lorries.
exercises.explain: The slow bike has the least, then the faster bike. A lorry has far more mass, so even at 30 km/h it has more than either bike, and the lorry at 60 km/h has the most.

exercises.prompt: A toy car must roll as far as it can. Sort the choices: less energy lost to rubbing, or more?
exercises.hint: Rubbing turns kinetic energy into heat. Which choices rub less?
exercises.explain: Oiled wheels, a smooth ramp and round wheels rub less, so the car keeps more kinetic energy. A rusty axle, a carpet and sticky tyres rub more, turning it into heat.

exercises.prompt: A pendulum has 10 units of energy, all stored at the top. Halfway down, 6 units are kinetic. How many units are still stored there?
exercises.hint: Energy is never lost: the stored and the kinetic parts add up to the same total.
exercises.explain: The total stays 10 units. Halfway down, 6 are kinetic, so 10 − 6 = 4 are still stored. At the bottom all 10 are kinetic (if nothing is lost to rubbing).
